ISSUE NO.1 8.

It is pertinent to mention here that as per settled proposition of law, in an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.

Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Sakshi Bhutani & Others., MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012, Bimla Devi & Others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand & Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018, Law Suit (SC) 303.
9.

sentences.text: In order to prove the case, petitioner No.2 being eye- witness of the accident examined himself as PW2.

PW2 Rakesh Kanojia testified that on 09.05.2018, he had seen accident and also apprehended the driver of the offending vehicle with the help of public person and further that he had informed police at 100 number.

He deposed that he was waiting at the gate of Police Station, Ashok Nagar to meet his brother Rajesh with regard to some dispute, for which he had to lodge the complaint with the _____________________________________________________________ police.
He also deposed that the motorcycle on which he was travelling had been borrowed from his acquaintance and further that he chased the offending vehicle, as deceased had died on the spot.
PW2 deposed that the driver of the offending vehicle was driving at a high speed and hit the deceased from behind.
PW2 was cross
- examined at length by learned counsel for the insurance company but nothing favourable to the respondents could be elicited.
Offending vehicle was seized from the spot on the date of accident itself, as reflected through seizure memo attached with DAR as part of charge-sheet.
Mechanical Inspection Report, which is part of charge-sheet and attached with the DAR, reflects accidental impact and several fresh damages were found present on the vehicle.
PW2 has specified that he had made call to police about the accident.
He denied being a planted witness.
FIR was lodged without delay.
PW2 deposed that driving by R1 was negligent and specified that R1 was driving at high speed and hit the victim from behind.

R1 was arrested from the spot and documents of his vehicle and his driving license were seized on the same day as reflected through Puran Chand vs Nand Kishore on 13 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/36193556/
4 the charge-sheet, which is a part of DAR.

Thus, in view of the above, this Tribunal is of the opinion that petitioners have been able to prove that there is sufficient material on record to establish that the accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by respondent no.1 and that resulted into grievous injuries to the deceased victim Dilip Kumar @ Dilip.
Therefore, issue no.1 is decided in favour of petitioners.
In view of the finding on issue no.1, petitioners are entitled to get compensation, however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.

COMPUTATION OF COMPENSATION 12. Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance
A man is not compensated for the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v. Willoughby (1970) Ac 467 at page 492 per Lord Reid).
13. The scope of compensation in injury cases has been considered by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Mr. R.D. Hattangadi v. M/S Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd., 1995 AIR 755.

The relevant extract is as under:
"Broadly speaking while fixing an amount of compensation payable to a victim of an accident, the damages have to be assessed separately as pecuniary damages and special damages.

Pecuniary damages are those which the victim has actually incurred and which is capable of being calculated in terms of money-, whereas non-pecuniary damages are those which are incapable of being assessed by arithmetical calculations.

(iii) other material loss.

So far non- pecuniary damages are concerned, they may include (i) damages for mental and physical shock, pain suffering, already suffered or likely to be suffered in future;
(ii) damages to compensate for the loss of amenities of life which may include a variety of matters i.e. on account of injury the claimant may not be able to walk, run or sit; (iii) damages for the loss of expectation of life, i.e. on account of injury the normal longevity of the person concerned is shortened; (iv) inconvenience,

The relevant paras of the judgment are reproduced as under:
4.

The provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident.
The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.

The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which _____________________________________________________________ he suffered as a result of such injury.

This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned.

5. The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following:
Pecuniary Damages (special damages)

(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation,
nourishing food and miscellaneous expenditure.

(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising:
(a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment.
(b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
(iii) Future medical expenses.

Non-Pecuniary Damages (general  damages)
 (iv) Damages to pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.

6  (v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of  prospects of marriage)
(vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity).
In routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under heads (i), (ii), (a) and (iv).

It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii), (b), (iii), (v)
and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, _____________________________________________________________ loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life.

The Income of deceased is being taken as per the minimum wages applicable to a semi-skilled worker applicable in Delhi on the date of accident i.e. Rs. 15,296/- per month.

Since the deceased Dilip Kumar @ Dilip was under the age of 40 years, prospects to the tune of 40% shall be added to his income in view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi and Ors. (AIR 2017 SC 5157).

19.
The wife of the deceased namely Kanta is stated to have predeceased him and her death-certificate is placed on record E x .
Therefore,
1/3rd of the income of deceased has to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.
The monthly income of the deceased has been assessed at Rs.15,296/-.
This means that the annual income of the deceased was Rs.15,296x12= Rs1,83,552/-.
After adding future prospects at the rate of 40%, this yearly income will become Rs.2,56,972/-
(Rs.1,83,552+ Rs.73,420).
After deduction of 1/3rd of his personal & living expenses amounting to Rs.85,657/-, the yearly income will remain as Rs.1,71,314/- (2/3rd of of Rs.2,56,972/-).
Applying the multiplier of 15, the loss of dependency is computed as Rs.25,69,710/- (Rs.1,71,314x15).
NON-PECUNIARY DAMAGES:
21.
In view of the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court, dated 31.10.2017, in case of National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi and Ors. (AIR 2017 SC 5157), a compensation of Rs.40,000/-, 15,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively has been fixed on account of loss of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses and further, it is required to be enhanced @ 10% in every three years.
Therefore, a compensation of Rs. 44,000/-
each to the father, son and daughter of the deceased on account of loss of consortium, 16,500/- and Rs.16,500/- respectively on account of loss of estate and funeral expenses to all the petitioners c o l l e c t i v e l y i s r e q u i r e d t o b e g r a n t e d .
22. In view of above, petitioners shall be entitled for total compensation i.e., Rs. 27,34,710/-
(25,69,710/-+ 1,65,000/-).
No medical expenses were incurred or claimed and hence, no compensation is being awarded for the same.
It is observed that vide order dt. 05.04.2019, an interim award for the sum of Rs.
50,000/- was passed in favour of the petitioners in view of Section 140 of M.V. Act and this amount has to be adjusted and deducted from the total compensation awarded.
24.

 Head of claim Amount In Rs.
 Loss of Dependency Rs. 25,69,710/-
 after applying  multiplier of 15  Loss of consortium Rs.44,000/- each to the petitioners  or Loss of love and amounting to Rs.1,32,000 /-
 affection Conventional Heads Rs.16,500+16,500=Rs.33,000/-
 (Funeral Expense  and loss of estate  Award Rs.27,34,710-50,000 (interim  compensation)= 26, 84,710/-
 (Rounded off to Rs.26,85,000/-)

25. Petitioners have pursued the case since 18.12.2018.
Accordingly, petitioners shall be entitled for interest @ 7.5% per annum on the aforesaid award amount from the date of filing of the petition till realisation.
LIABILITY:
As insurance company has contractual and statutory liability to indemnify the insured and,
in this case, insurance company has not been able to prove that any term or condition of insurance policy was breached/ violated by insured, therefore, respondent no.2/ insurance company namely United of Insurance Company Ltd. becomes liable to pay the aforesaid compensation amount.
In view of the findings on above points, I as presiding officer of this Tribunal award a total compensation of Rs.26,85,000/- (Rs.Twenty Six Lakhs Eighty Five Thousand only) along with interest @ 7.5 % per annum on the aforesaid award amount from the date of filing of the petition till realisation except for the period mentioned above, in favour of petitioners and against the Puran Chand vs Nand Kishore on 13 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/36193556/
